Gnädigster Fürst und Herr!

Hier nach Läute der Congress um wohl noch ehenden als in 3 Woche, seine Endſchaft erreicht haben,
aber nun fängt Engeland neue und ganz teuflische Intragnie an - diese Waßer hände
wollen Oſt Friesland haben, und wir ſollen, dafür Dannemarck entschädigen.
der Kayser Allexander dringt auf unserm König ein daß dem Vice Königl. von Italien ein

translation.en: Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! As concerns Poland, matters have now only got so far that the frontier has been agreed from the territory of Thorn onward, by way of Slupce near Peisern, across the Wartha and down the Prosna as far as Saoleslawiae, over against [uncertain: Pitschum]. Likewise the frontier for the Saxony that is to remain has also been fixed. The King of Saxony, who yesterday was invited to come hither by an Austrian and a Prussian courier, keeps Dresden, Leipzig and Bautzen. According to this, the Congress will indeed have reached its end sooner rather than in 3 weeks; but now England begins new and quite devilish intrigues — these water-hands want to have East Friesland, and we are to compensate Denmark for it. The Emperor Alexander presses upon our King that a piece of land on our side in Germany is to be given to the Viceroy of Italy. Both matters will draw the most obstinate debates after them, for, as people say, the King will by no means suffer this. When thereafter the affairs of the German Empire are still to be arranged in general, when everything must be painted 15 times over on parchment, then many an hour more of time will still be required. Be that as it may, I go on plaguing the Prince Chancellor, yet he still remains good throughout and his patience will not tire — The papers still lie with the Privy Councillor of State Stägemann. It is true enough that the work is frightfully great, but I keep on admonishing; thus, for example, I have again submitted to the Prince a petition as the figure shows — He received it graciously and promised certainly to help — Everyone of the good sort of men holds the matter of the 112000 Rthl advance to be quite certain and settled; with Cosmar himself it will probably drag out somewhat, for the Prince will punish the business severely, the more so as the report of the Brieg Superior Court of Justice has turned out so favourably.

B: is very active and handles the matter wisely and restlessly — All honest souls wish that Prince August would only quickly revoke the power of attorney given to Cosmar, and in doing so enter into no pour parlez with the pettifogger, but rather, as I have already advised, write to the Minister of Justice and to the Brieger O L Court that he has revoked the power of attorney given to Cosmar. Once this has been done, the 112000 Rthl paid over and the Curian heirs satisfied therewith, then Cosmar is thrown down — the Board of Wards, as also the Brieger O.L. Court, will bury him outright, especially if the guardianship in respect of Adolph is taken from him. As regards the Polish estates I await the decision at every moment — whether I am to come away or whether the Prince Chancellor will settle the matter alone. From von Pourtales B. expects the answer in 10 to 12 days. B wishes that 6. might not come sooner than towards the end of April, because until then the work would still be dreadfully much — and o. would not gladly wish to settle the matter without him. From the King there lies a letter for Your Serene Highness in the field post — It is presumably the answer to your New Year's congratulation. With the greatest respect I remain Your Serene Highness's Vienna, the 13th of February 1815 wholly most obedient servant v Triebenfeld

Be that as it may, I go on plaguing the Prince Chancellor, yet he still remains good throughout and his patience will not tire — The papers still lie with the Privy Councillor of State Stägemann. It is true enough that the work is frightfully great, but I keep on admonishing; thus, for example, I have again submitted to the Prince a petition as the figure shows — He received it graciously and promised certainly to help — Everyone of the good sort of men holds the matter of the 112000 Rthl advance to be quite certain and settled; with Cosmar himself it will probably drag out somewhat, for the Prince will punish the business severely, the more so as the report of the Brieg Superior Court of Justice has turned out so favourably.

B: is very active and handles the matter wisely and restlessly — All honest souls wish that Prince August would only quickly revoke the power of attorney given to Cosmar, and in doing so enter into no pour parlez with the pettifogger, but rather, as I have already advised, write to the Minister of Justice and to the Brieger O L Court that he has revoked the power of attorney given to Cosmar. Once this has been done, the 112000 Rthl paid over and the Curian heirs satisfied therewith, then Cosmar is thrown down — the Board of Wards, as also the Brieger O.L. Court, will bury him outright, especially if the guardianship in respect of Adolph is taken from him. As regards the Polish estates I await the decision at every moment — whether I am to come away or whether the Prince Chancellor will settle the matter alone. From von Pourtales B. expects the answer in 10 to 12 days. B wishes that 6. might not come sooner than towards the end of April, because until then the work would still be dreadfully much — and o. would not gladly wish to settle the matter without him. From the King there lies a letter for Your Serene Highness in the field post — It is presumably the answer to your New Year's congratulation. With the greatest respect I remain Your Serene Highness's Vienna, the 13th of February 1815 wholly most obedient servant v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Reports from the Congress that the Polish frontier has been settled from Thorn by Slupce near Peisern across the Wartha and down the Prosna, and Saxony's border fixed, the King keeping Dresden, Leipzig and Bautzen; England now demands East Friesland and Alexander presses land for the Viceroy of Italy. Triebenfeld keeps pressing the Prince Chancellor and Stägemann; the 112000 Rthl advance is thought secure, and Prince August should revoke Cosmar's power of attorney.
summary_de: Bericht vom Wiener Congress: die Grenze Polens sei von Thorn über Slupce bei Peisern, über die Wartha und die Prosna bis Saoleslawiae festgelegt, ebenso die Grenze für das verbleibende Sachsen, dessen König Dresden, Leipzig und Bautzen behalte; England fordere Ostfriesland, Kaiser Alexander Land für den Vicekönig von Italien. Triebenfeld dränge den Fürsten Staatskanzler; die Papiere lägen bei Geheimen Staatsrath Stägemann. Der Vorschuß von 112000 Rthl gelte als gesichert; Prinz August solle die Cosmar erteilte Vollmacht widerrufen und dies dem Justizminister und dem Brieger O L Gericht anzeigen. Entscheidung über die polnischen Güter erwartet.
